texts.preamble: Harshavarna K H vs Malleshappa M B on 15 November, 2025 Kabc020425002023 In The Court Of Xxi Addl.Small Cause Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (Scch-23) Dated This The 15th Day Of November - 2025 Present: Sri. Shreyansh Doddamani B.Com. Ll.B (Spl), Xxi Addl. Scj & Acjm Member - Mact, Bengaluru. MVC.No.8352/2023 C/W MVC.No.8353/2023
texts.facts: These claim petitions are filed under Section 166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident. As both petitions were arising out of the same accident, they were clubbed together for recording of common evidence and judgment. 2. The common facts leading to the filing of the top noted petitions are that on 24.11.2023 at about 8.40 a.m, when the petitioner in MVC-8352/2023 being accompanied by three pillion riders i.e., along with his wife and 2 children was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-EY-6994 near Urdigere Circle, Koratagere Town, Tumkur District, the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-H-5054 came at high speed in a rash & negligent manner and dashed against their motorcycle. Due to the tremendous impact they fell down and sustained grievous injuries. After the accident both the petitioners were shifted to Government Hospital, Koratagere, wherein they took first aid and thereafter they were shifted to District Hospital, Tumkur wherein they took treatment as an outpatient and thereafter they took treatment as an inpatient at Aruna Hospital. They are still under treatment and have spent considerable amount towards their medicines, conveyance and other incidental Harshavarna K H vs Malleshappa M B on 15 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110173407/ 2 expenses. On account of the accidental injuries the petitioners have suffered permanent disablement. The respondent 4 SCCH-23 MVC.8352/2023 C/w MVC.8353/2023 No.1and 2 being the owner and insurer of the car thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation. 3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal. Hence he was placed exparte. 4. The respondent No.2 filed written statement admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car. However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms and conditions of the policy. This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident. Negligence on the part of the driver of insured vehicle is denied by this respondent. Per contra it is alleged that the rider of motorcycle/ petitioner in MVC.8352/2023 who was riding the said vehicle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident. It is further contended that as per the police documents there are four persons including the 5 SCCH-23 MVC.8352/2023 C/w MVC.8353/2023 injured were traveling on a two wheeler, it amounts to violation of section 128 of the MV Act. In the event of carrying more than one pillion rider on a motorcycle each one of them Harshavarna K H vs Malleshappa M B on 15 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110173407/ 3 was contributed negligence in causing the accident. It is self negligence case as such the claim petition was not maintainable. Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL and further the said insured vehicle did not holding valid and effective Permit and FC. Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver. On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him. Further denied all the allegation made in the petition. Hence prayed to dismiss the petitions. 5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues (which are common in both petitions) were framed: 6 SCCH-23 MVC.8352/2023 C/w MVC.8353/2023 ISSUES 1. Ex's .P1 to P13 and Ex.P.19 & 20 were marked on his behalf. The petitioner in MVC.No.8352/2023 got examined herself as PW.2. Ex's . P14 to 18 and Ex.P.21 were marked Harshavarna K H vs Malleshappa M B on 15 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110173407/ 4 through him. The Public Relation Officer at Aruna Hospital, Tumkur was examined as PW.3 (in both the petitions). Ex's . P22 to 24 were marked through this witness. Dr.S.A. Somashekara Orthopedics Surgeon was examined as PW.3 (in both the petitions). Ex's .P25 to 28 were marked through this witness. In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 examined the FDA at Bengaluru Central RTO as RW.1 and 7 SCCH-23 MVC.8352/2023 C/w MVC.8353/2023 through him Ex.R.1 to 3 were marked. Further the respondent No.2 also examined the FDA, RTO, Tumkur as RW.2 and through him Ex.R.4 to 7 were marked. Further more the respondent No.2 insurance company got examined its concerned officer as RW.3. Ex. R.8 and 9 were marked through him. My findings on the above said issues are as under : Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative (in both the petitions) Issue No.2 (in both the petitions) : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order (in both the petitions) for the following:- REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 (IN BOTH THE PETITIONS): The evidence on record reveals that one Srirangaiah lodged the complaint about the occurrence of accident with Koratagere police. After receipt of the complaint the said police registered an FIR Harshavarna K H vs Malleshappa M B on 15 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110173407/ 5 against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AH-5054 and 8 SCCH-23 MVC.8352/2023 C/w MVC.8353/2023 took up investigation. During the course of investigation material evidence connected to the accident was collected by them. The Wound certificates marked at Ex's.P5 and 14 disclose that the petitioners sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
texts.arguments: He has thereby opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said vehicles. Therefore the driver of the car did not have sufficient cause to have lost control of his vehicle. Such being the case, the very fact that he dashed against the motorcycle on which the petitioners were proceeding leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving his vehicle rashly & negligently. Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under section's 279, 337 & 338 of 9 SCCH-23 MVC.8352/2023 C/w MVC.8353/2023 IPC. There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive. 9. During the course of cross-examination of PW.1 & 2, the learned counsel for insurance company could not elicit Harshavarna K H vs Malleshappa M B on 15 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110173407/ 6 anything worthwhile to negate their testimonies. Apart from that perusal of the written statement filed by the respondent No.2 shows that the insurance company has taken divergent stands. At one stretch it has denied the very involvement of its insured vehicle and at another it has contended that there was no negligence on the part of driver of its insured vehicle. Thus, absolutely there is no merit in the defence taken by respondent No.2. The main contention of the insurance company is that the petitioner in MVC.8352/2023 (PW.1) who was riding his motorcycle with three persons on the pillion, has contributed his negligence in the occurrence of the accident. However the fact that PW.1 was riding a motorcycle accompanied by three pillion riders, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence. At the most, he would be guilty of being a party to the violation of 10 SCCH-23 MVC.8352/2023 C/w MVC.8353/2023 law. But such violation by itself, without anything more, cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence unless it is established that it is the very act of PW.1 riding along with there others contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon him and the other petitioners. 10. In this regard the respondnet No.2 relied the decision reported in 2003 0 Supreme (AP) 1460, in case of United India Insurance Company Limited v/s K. Anjaiah. Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Andhra Pradesh held that, in this case admittedly there is triple riding and can be presumed that Harshavarna K H vs Malleshappa M B on 15 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110173407/ 7 rider of scooter was discomforted by reason of allowing two pillion riders and thus contributed in causing accident - As such, culpability in causing accident is fixed at 75% on part of driver of accident lorry and 25% on part of rider of scooter - Appeal, partly allowed. 11. Further it is relied on the decision reported in AIR 2003 Karnataka 258 in the case of P.S. Somaiah and another 11 SCCH-23 MVC.8352/2023 C/w MVC.8353/2023 v/s . Wherein it is held that, "(A) Motor Vehicles Act (59 of 1988), S.128 - Driving of two - wheelers - Carriage of children in any position in front of rider - Is totally prohibited - State Authorities directed to take steps for enforcement of safety measures - Court also issued clear warning that in case of its failure to do so Court will be required to hold State liable in appropriate cases." 12. As held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Mohammed Siddique and another V/s National Insurance Co.Ltd and Others 'There must either be causal connection between the violation and the accident or a causal connection between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim. It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. As such this Court is taking the notional income as prescribed Harshavarna K H vs Malleshappa M B on 15 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110173407/ 10 by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru. Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343. Per contra the learned advocate for petitioner relied on the decision of Honble High Court of Delhi in Guruneeth Singh V/s New India Ass.Co.Ltd., and others reported in 2023 SCC Online Del 6269. He also relied on the case of Amrit Paul Singh V/s Tata AIG General Insurance Company Ltd., and Others reported in (2018) 7 SCC 558 the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that even when there is violation of permit Harshavarna K H vs Malleshappa M B on 15 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110173407/ 20 conditions, the insurer is liable to satisfy the award with a 28 SCCH-23 41 . On the other hand advocate for respondent argued that it was before amendment of MV Act 2019. The advocate for petitioner has relied on the decision in the case of Branch Manager, SBI Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd, V/s Muthulakshmi and others reported in 2025 ACJ 1925. Wherein Hon'ble High Court of Madras held that not withstanding the deletion of proviso to sub section 4 and sub section 5 of old section 149 of M.V.Act, 1988 by amending at 30.02.2019 does not abrogate insurers statutory liability under sub section 1 to satisfy the award to third parties of victims and the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal can pass orders for pay and recover.
